name: playcraft
title: PLAYCRAFT — game design and gameplay quality
summary: Assesses and improves how a game plays. Reads the repo (intent, engine, controls, systems with file:line evidence, genres across 15 genre profiles), plays the built game in Chromium on desktop and phone (response time of every control, dead time, idle motion, FPS, pause, touch targets, text size), scores 10 categories 0-100 with evidence levels (verified / observed / inferred / not tested) and confidence, ranks the highest-impact opportunities by impact, effort and risk, writes a staged plan, then verifies changes against the baseline (regressions + guardrails on the git diff) with a before/after report. full_pass adds GITCRAFT's engineering checks (TestCraft) under one plan.
output_license: Reports generated by GITCRAFT; owned by the requesting project

limits: Builds are not run inside the sandbox (no package registry): build the game with its own toolchain first and pass target=<dist>.
Chromium renders WebGL in software (SwiftShader): FPS is relative and scored as observed; test on a real phone before claiming device performance.

Response time is measured from the screen (64×36 canvas samples each frame + DOM mutations) against an idle baseline: accurate to a frame for games that wait for input, approximate for games that animate constantly.

The probe plays generically (keys from the source, taps, drags, a seeded mixed session). Game-specific goals (finishing a level) need start_steps, exposed state (window.__game) or the project's own scripted playtests passed as evidence.
Design quality (is the loop compelling?) cannot be measured automatically: record it as judgements with evidence; unplayed or judgement-free categories stay low-confidence and capped.
PLAYCRAFT does not edit games: phase 5 is done in the game repo by the caller following the plan; verify then checks the result.
